summary: Say the counting numbers in order, working up to 20.
See how many are in a small group, up to 5, without counting.
Count things one by one, and know the last number said tells how many.
Compare two groups: which has more, which has fewer, or the same.

See, copy and continue simple repeating patterns.

Name and compare shapes of any size or turn, and put shapes together.
Describe where things are: above, below, beside, in front, behind.
Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
Count forward from any number, not just 1.
Write numbers 0–20 and use a numeral to show how many.

Count up to 20 objects in a line or a group, and count out a given number.

Compare two written numbers between 1 and 10.

Break numbers up to 10 into pairs in more than one way.
Find the number that makes 10 with any number from 1 to 9.

Sort objects into groups and count each group.
Describe where things are: above, below, beside, in front of, behind, next to.

Tell flat shapes from solid shapes.

Build and draw shapes.
Put small shapes together to make bigger ones.
Solve adding and subtracting story problems within 20.
Solve story problems that add three numbers, with a sum within 20.
Use turn-around facts and grouping to make adding easier.
Think of subtraction as finding a missing addend.
Connect counting on and counting back to adding and subtracting.
Add and subtract within 20 using strategies like making ten and doubles.

Find the missing number in an addition or subtraction equation.

Compare two-digit numbers using >, = and <.
Add within 100 using models and place value.
Find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number in your head.

Put shapes together to make new shapes.
Split circles and rectangles into halves and fourths.
Solve one- and two-step adding and subtracting story problems within 100.
Add and subtract within 20 from memory.

Use repeated addition to count objects in rows and columns.

Compare three-digit numbers using >, = and <.
Add and subtract within 100 using place value.
Add up to four two-digit numbers.
Add and subtract within 1000 using models and place value.
Add or subtract 10 or 100 in your head, for numbers 100–900.
Explain why adding and subtracting strategies work.
Measure length with a ruler, yardstick, meter stick or tape.
Measure something twice with different units and compare the numbers.
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters and meters.
Measure how much longer one object is than another.
Solve length story problems within 100.
Show numbers, sums and differences on a number line.

Solve money problems with dollars, quarters, dimes, nickels and pennies.

Draw picture graphs and bar graphs with up to four categories.
Recognize and draw shapes by their angles and faces.
Split a rectangle into rows and columns of equal squares and count them.
Split circles and rectangles into two, three or four equal shares.

Solve multiplying and dividing story problems within 100.
Find the missing number in a multiplication or division equation.
Use turn-around facts and grouping to multiply.

Solve two-step story problems using all four operations.
Find and explain patterns in addition and multiplication tables.
Round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.
Add and subtract within 1000.
Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10.

Draw scaled picture and bar graphs and answer how-many-more questions.

Solve perimeter problems, including finding a missing side.
